issues.description: Event-5 gap filling grows in the wrong chemical direction. Lower template is 5'(left)->3'(right), so the nascent lagging strand must elongate right->left (its 3' end is at the left, as the video's own lbl_lag3 and Okazaki-1 growth correctly show). Measured fill additions go left->right (x=2.092 -> 2.275 -> 2.458), i.e. projections on the template-reading vector [-1,0] are negative (-0.183, -0.183). This depicts 3'->5' addition / extension from a 5' phosphate end. Correct repair: nucleate fill at the 3' end of the downstream fragment (okazaki_fragment_2 side, larger x) and add successively toward smaller x.

artifact_evidence.observation: Green fill blocks appear first at the LEFT edge of the ex-primer gap (~x=2.09) and then progressively to the right (~2.28, ~2.46) between 28.5 s and 29.1 s; frame 29.2 s shows the left part of the gap filled and the right part still empty.

issues.description: Ligase is placed at the right edge of the removed primer (x=2.55) but the neighbouring downstream DNA (okazaki_fragment_2, left edge x=2.86) is not adjacent: an unfilled spacer remains. The red nick marker therefore marks a gap, not a nick, and ligase is shown sealing across missing nucleotides. Ligase correctly adds no DNA, but a nick requires juxtaposed 3'-OH/5'-P after complete fill; the final 'Local copied duplexes' frame still shows an open gap between the two green runs.

artifact_evidence.observation: Gold ligase sits over a red tick at the right end of the left green run; at 31.2-32.2 s a clear black gap still separates that run from the next green+orange fragment.

issues.description: The central blue hollow ladder (make_duplex at y=0, x=0.55..6.0) is never registered and carries no polarity labels or parental annotation. Because both blue templates run essentially full width (x=-5.8..5.9) at y=+/-1.35 and never converge into it, the ladder reads as an ADDITIONAL third double-stranded DNA floating between two already-separated strands rather than the unreplicated parental duplex ahead of the fork. Identity cannot be confirmed from the picture: parental duplex vs. extra DNA is UNCERTAIN.

artifact_evidence.observation: Two near-horizontal blue lines span the whole frame; a separate runged blue ladder sits mid-right at y=0; a single vertical blue bar at x~0.5 is the only 'fork' connection. No Y convergence, no label on the ladder.

issues.description: The fork junction never moves and the parental ladder never shortens, yet all nascent synthesis (leading to x=4.9; lagging primers at x=2.0 and 3.7) is drawn to the RIGHT of the junction, i.e. along the same x-range still occupied by the intact parental duplex. This depicts polymerase copying duplex DNA without unwinding, and makes 'nearer the advancing fork' for primer 2 meaningless. Either advance the junction rightward while shortening the parental ladder, or move all nascent strands to the already-open (left) side.

artifact_evidence.observation: Vertical fork bar stays at the same x from 1.2 s to 32.2 s; the mid-right ladder keeps constant length while green/orange blocks accumulate to its right-hand x-range on both templates.

issues.description: The leading-strand polymerase is labelled 'Pol delta' throughout event 3/4. Per F4 the model supported by the preponderance of evidence assigns bulk leading-strand synthesis at an undisturbed fork to Pol epsilon; Pol delta is the lagging-strand elongation/maturation enzyme (F6). Using the same glyph and the same 'Pol delta' label for leading, lagging and fill enzymes collapses a distinction the scene is meant to teach.

artifact_evidence.observation: Cyan clamp-shaped enzyme on the upper template is captioned 'Pol delta' and keeps that label while extending the leading strand rightward.

issues.description: dna_polymerase_fill is placed statically above the gap centre with no registered active-site anchor and no bind_near; it does not track the end where nucleotides appear. Proximity passes only because the gap is short (0.55-0.58 scene units). Even after the direction fix, the enzyme must stay anchored to the moving 3' growing end.

artifact_evidence.observation: Fill polymerase remains at one fixed position above the gap while green blocks appear sequentially beneath it.

issues.description: Closing caption 'Local copied duplexes' overstates completion: the leading RNA primer (orange, upper left) and the whole lagging-2 RNA primer are still present, and a gap remains in the lagging strand. Either restrict the caption to 'one nick sealed locally' or complete primer removal/fill for the shown fragments.

artifact_evidence.observation: Final frame: orange blocks persist on both nascent strands and a black gap persists between the two lower green runs.

issues.description: Primase alone is shown making the RNA primer and Pol delta then extends directly; the Pol alpha initiation step (F5) is not represented or labelled. Acceptable simplification only if the caption does not imply primase alone initiates Okazaki DNA synthesis; identity of the initiating polymerase remains UNCERTAIN on screen.

artifact_evidence.observation: Purple primase appears below the lower template, orange primer blocks appear, primase leaves, cyan 'Pol delta' arrives; no Pol alpha object or label at any time.

checks.reason: Upper 3'(left)/5'(right) vs lower 5'(left)/3'(right) are antiparallel and stay fixed all 32 s.
Leading primer 3' label at its right end and nascent growth left->right give 5'->3' synthesis antiparallel to the upper template; trajectory 9.3-14.0 s confirms rightward addition.
Fragments 1 and 2 elongate leftward from their own RNA 3' ends (x decreasing), with 3' label at the left end; consistent with lagging polarity.
Measured fill order increases x (2.092->2.275->2.458) against template-reading vector [-1,0]; negative projections. Trajectory, not sparse frames, establishes the reversal.
Observed order is primer fade (~24.5 s) -> gap label -> fill (~28.5-29.1 s) -> ligase (~30.2 s); ligase adds no nucleotides. Order alone does not rescue the direction/adjacency defects.
Sealed position x=2.55 is not juxtaposed to downstream DNA starting at x=2.86; a gap remains at 32.2 s.
Unregistered central ladder plus full-width parallel templates: cannot decide parental duplex vs additional DNA from the picture; no Y junction and no fork motion.
All sampled additions within 0.55-0.73 scene units of their polymerase (<1.1 threshold); schematic proximity only, not biochemical contact.
Provided GRID image contains unrelated SVM lecture content; used only as coordinate reference and excluded from scientific judgement.
